history.period: Antiquity uncertain; idol believed centuries old
history.summary: The Chaturvuj Narayan Mandir in Piro, Bhojpur district, is a shrine to the four-armed form of Lord Vishnu, holding the Sudarshana Chakra, Panchajanya conch, Kaumodaki mace and Padma lotus. Its ancient stone idol of Lakshmi-Narayan is locally believed to have been discovered during an excavation centuries ago and then enshrined; the architecture is North Indian style with a prominent shikhara and pillars carved with Dashavatara scenes. It is the spiritual hub of the Piro block, with daily aarti/bhajans and its biggest gatherings on Kartik Purnima and Vaikuntha Ekadashi. NOTE: CSV town 'Arrah' is wrong - the temple is in Piro town, ~30 km southwest of Arrah (correct town given). The excavation/age claims come from a single tourism listing and are unverified. Coordinates are Piro town (approximate).

name: Chaturvuj Narayan Mandir
town_description: Piro is a town and nagar panchayat in Bhojpur district, Bihar, about 30 km southwest of Arrah; an agricultural market town serving the surrounding Piro block.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (~90 km).
travel.railway: Piro railway station on the Ara-Sasaram line; Ara Junction (~30 km) is the nearest major railhead.
travel.road: About 30 km southwest of Arrah, reached by bus/taxi via the Ara-Sasaram road.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Kartik Purnima for the main festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM to 8:30 PM daily; closed 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM (per tourism listing - verify).
